prediction.likelyOutcome: Liability is conceded, so the bench trial will turn entirely on damages methodology. The landlord's $538,000 acceleration theory is undercut by the lease's own conditional language (acceleration applies only 'if Landlord does not relet') and by the landlord's own reletting/offset conduct, so a deficiency-based rent award closer to Kolaj's $78,000-$96,000 calculation (adjusted for additional elapsed time) is more likely than full acceleration. The $300,000 kitchen claim is the weakest component given the total absence of valuation testimony at trial and is unlikely to be sustained in any significant amount. Attorneys' fees and late fees/interest are comparatively secure. Net expected recovery is likely well below the $905,000 requested, in the range described below.

issues.label: Base Deficiency Rent Recovery (Unpaid Rent Net of Reletting)
Incremental Recovery if Full Acceleration Theory Prevails

outcome.description: After the bench trial the trial court rendered judgment for the landlord of $96,072.49 (unpaid rent through trial net of replacement-tenant rent, late fees, and prejudgment interest) — the figure the tenant advocated, roughly one-tenth of the more than $900,000 the landlord sought — plus 18% post-judgment interest, and awarded $0 in attorneys' fees. The court of appeals affirmed the damages award and reversed only the denial of attorneys' fees, remanding for a determination of a reasonable fee under the lease.
outcome.finalNote: Damages affirmed; fee denial reversed and remanded.
